sources.label: MUSD Ethereum exact Sourcify source and ABI

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The exact MUSD source and Ethereum ABI show that addToBurnList(address) is onlyOwner and burn(account, amount) checks only burnList[msg.sender], then burns the specified account without that account's approval or allowance. At Ethereum block 25534618, Base block 48643892, and Mezo block 10403815, owner() returned 0x98D8899c3030741925BE630C710A98B57F397C7a and burnList(owner) returned false on all three deployments; their 6,436-byte runtime layouts differ only in a 34-byte chain-specific range. The current owner can therefore grant arbitrary-account burn ability on each deployment. transfer and transferFrom have no separate blacklist or pause check, but this owner-grantable burn path is direct individual holder impairment.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 access review

oracleRisk.summary: Mezo MUSD uses one BTC collateral path whose PriceFeed reads a single Chainlink-compatible BTC/USD oracle, rejects data older than 60 seconds, and supplies the price to Liquity-style trove liquidation.

branchApplicability.rationale: MUSD is issued from BTC-backed borrower troves with a 110% minimum collateral ratio. Mezo's published contracts use one shared PriceFeed, TroveManager, StabilityPool, and redistribution engine for that BTC collateral path, so one complete branch row covers the liquidation surface.

branches.label: Mezo BTC troves
branches.summary: All MUSD troves use the shared Mezo PriceFeed BTC/USD answer to calculate individual collateral ratios and liquidation eligibility.

feeds.provider: Mezo PriceFeed with Chainlink-compatible Skip Connect BTC/USD oracle
feeds.path: Skip Connect BTC/USD answer -> Mezo PriceFeed.fetchPrice -> TroveManager ICR

branches.fallbackBehavior: PriceFeed.fetchPrice reverts when the configured oracle answer is more than 60 seconds old or the oracle call fails. The contract has no secondary source or stored last-good-price fallback; the owner can replace the configured oracle through setOracle.

collateralParameters.note: A trove becomes liquidatable when its individual collateral ratio falls below the fixed 110% MCR.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Any caller may submit one or more active troves for immediate liquidation. TroveManager first offsets principal and interest against MUSD in the StabilityPool, transfers proportional BTC collateral to the pool, and redistributes any uncovered debt and collateral to remaining active troves.
branches.backstop: The MUSD StabilityPool is the first-loss backstop and is seeded by protocol-controlled value; StabilityPool deposits burn against liquidated debt and receive the seized BTC collateral.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Debt exceeding available StabilityPool MUSD is redistributed with its remaining collateral across active troves through the DefaultPool reward indices. A stale or failing oracle halts price-dependent liquidation by reverting, and the reviewed contracts do not implement a last-good-price or global shutdown settlement path.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: MUSD is natively issued only on Mezo through Liquity-style BTC-backed CDP and interest paths. Wormhole NTT v1.1.0 makes Mezo the locking hub and Ethereum and Base conserved burn-mint representations: their NTT managers can mint only from guardian-attested burns, while the shared 5-of-9 Safe administers token and manager roles, upgrades, pauses, peers, and route limits. The one-transceiver/threshold-1 Wormhole attestation path and all manager controls are assessed here as external-validated bridge risk, not native issuance.

protocols.name: Wormhole NTT
protocols.note: Mezo is the NTT locking hub (manager mode()=0, holds bridged-out MUSD); Ethereum and Base are burning spokes (manager mode()=1). Deployment topology from the issuer's ntt-bridge-musd-mainnet deployment.json, with each manager, peer, transceiver, rate-limit, and owner path re-verified on-chain 2026-08-16.

routes.reviewNote: Canonical home chain. On-chain reads via Mezo RPC (2026-08-16, block 11179505): token owner() = 0x98D8899c3030741925BE630C710A98B57F397C7a, a 171-byte Safe proxy whose getThreshold()=5 and getOwners()=9 on Ethereum; mintList(BorrowerOperations 0x44b1bac67dDA612a41a58AAf779143B181dEe031)=true and mintList(InterestRateManager 0x4a453700d157717Fe02fB62E7700ED7845048285)=true, the native Liquity-style CDP and accrued-interest routes. The Wormhole NTT manager 0x7efb386675d75280D39Aae42964A6776DE0ee0bD reads token()=MUSD and mode()=0 (locking hub); its escrow, peers, transceiver, rate limits, and owner controls are assessed in bridgeRouteRisk.controls.

Burning-spoke representation. At Ethereum block 25770834 (2026-08-16), mintList(0x5293158bf7a81ED05418DA497a80F7e6DBF4477E)=true on the MUSD deployment; the 209-byte Wormhole NTT manager reads token()=MUSD and mode()=1 (burning), matching the issuer's ntt-bridge-musd-mainnet deployment.json. It mints only from conserved guardian-attested NTT burn messages and is not an independent Ethereum-native MUSD liability system. The token owner is the same Mezo 5-of-9 Safe; manager upgrade, pause, peer, transceiver, and rate-limit controls are structured below.

Burning-spoke representation. At Base block 50066278 (2026-08-16), mintList(0x3EB418BdBE95b4b9cf465ecfBD8424685ACD1Bc1)=true on the MUSD deployment; the 209-byte Wormhole NTT manager reads token()=MUSD and mode()=1 (burning), matching the issuer's ntt-bridge-musd-mainnet deployment.json. It mints only from conserved guardian-attested NTT burn messages and is not an independent Base-native MUSD liability system. The token owner is the same Mezo 5-of-9 Safe; manager upgrade, pause, peer, transceiver, and rate-limit controls are structured below.

controls.label: MUSD Mezo Wormhole NTT locking-hub manager

routeChecks.lockboxOrEscrow: The Mezo manager is the Wormhole NTT locking hub (mode/getMode=0) and holds MUSD locked when supply leaves Mezo; reverse transfers burn MUSD on Ethereum or Base and unlock the conserved amount on Mezo.
routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: At Mezo block 11179505, peers bind Wormhole chain 2 Ethereum to 0x5293158bf7a81ED05418DA497a80F7e6DBF4477E and chain 30 Base to 0x3EB418BdBE95b4b9cf465ecfBD8424685ACD1Bc1.
routeChecks.rateLimits: The official manifest sets 10,000,000 MUSD inbound per peer and uint64.max-scaled outbound capacity (184467440737.09551615 MUSD); current Mezo capacities matched those configured values. These are route limits, not a global supply cap.

controls.evidence: At Mezo block 11179505 on 2026-08-16, manager 0x7efb386675d75280D39Aae42964A6776DE0ee0bD returned token()=MUSD and mode/getMode()=0 (locking), with one enabled transceiver 0x62DEeaFEe06c7442A21c93edeDc79A0cb5791C83, owner Safe 0x98D8899c3030741925BE630C710A98B57F397C7a, and manager pauser 0x40C7b9612B394212394EA860cACd0e176CA4Ae5B. The current implementation slot was 0xd0cbe9be1ab548eb93e5557649b236305874d4d0; EIP-1967 admin and beacon slots were zero. The manager is canonical-side bridge escrow and route-limit machinery, not an independent native minter.

controls.label: MUSD token and Wormhole NTT owner Safe

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The shared Safe owns the three NTT managers and can set their peers and transceivers. The reviewed peers are Mezo↔Ethereum (Wormhole chains 50↔2), Mezo↔Base (50↔30), and the corresponding Ethereum↔Base bindings.
routeChecks.attestorQuorum: Each manager currently has one enabled Wormhole transceiver and an attestation threshold of 1; the Safe can change the configured transceiver and threshold.
routeChecks.rateLimits: The owner can set inbound and outbound NTT limits. The official manifest and current reads show 10,000,000 MUSD inbound per peer and uint64.max-scaled outbound capacity (184467440737.09551615 MUSD) on all three managers; these are route controls, not a global supply cap.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The Safe owns MUSD and each NTT manager. It can upgrade each manager through its owner-only upgrade path, set peers/transceivers/thresholds/limits, transfer ownership, and pause managers; each manager also has pauser 0x40C7b9612B394212394EA860cACd0e176CA4Ae5B. The MUSD token deployments are immutable, and their EIP-1967 implementation/admin/beacon slots are zero.

controls.capDescription: The shared Safe can administer mintList on each MUSD deployment and can change NTT bridge managers, peers, transceivers, limits, and pause state. Its arbitrary-minter authority over canonical Mezo issuance is retained only in Mint Authority; this control records the same Safe's bridge scope over the three NTT routes.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770834 on 2026-08-16, owner() of the MUSD deployment was 0x98D8899c3030741925BE630C710A98B57F397C7a on Ethereum, Base, and Mezo; the owner is a 5-of-9 Safe with the 9 listed owners. The same Safe owns all three Wormhole NTT managers. Empty Safe module pagination was observed, but getGuard() reverted, so guard status remains unresolved and is recorded as unknown. This shared controller's bridge administration is scored here; the canonical Mezo arbitrary-minter surface remains separately represented in Mint Authority.

controls.label: MUSD Wormhole transceiver Guardian attestation domain

routeChecks.attestorQuorum: The Mezo, Ethereum, and Base managers each currently have one enabled Wormhole transceiver with NTT attestation threshold 1: 0x62DEeaFEe06c7442A21c93edeDc79A0cb5791C83, 0x147379A0174780570D07d70a14FB244EE5f2D786, and 0x15C465E7dF34f8cA06FDCae0569206cEDf3f4467. A single enabled transceiver/Guardian attestation is therefore sufficient for message approval on each route.
routeChecks.signingModel: Inbound spoke minting is based on external Wormhole Guardian-attested NTT messages, while outbound spoke transfers burn MUSD and the Mezo hub releases the conserved locked amount. The off-chain Guardian signer roster and operational quorum were not independently enumerated in this review.
routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The deployed NTT managers bind the reviewed Mezo, Ethereum, and Base peers; the owner Safe can change those peer and transceiver bindings.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The deployment manifest records transceiver pauser 0x123694886DBf5Ac94DDA07135349534536D14cAf on each chain. Manager pauser 0x40C7b9612B394212394EA860cACd0e176CA4Ae5B is recorded on the manager controls; the external Guardian validation domain remains a common-mode dependency for all three routes.
